findings.summary: The first wall is the faintest mark in the picture at 2.583:1 against white, below the 3:1 the repository's style asks of a line on white and lighter than the coil grey it is set against (3.112:1), while the cell mesh it sits over measures a median 4.616 to 4.704:1. The mechanism the node claims is present and visible: the dash renders, the legend swatch repeats it, and the wall is drawn above the clipped cell outlines, crossing them in the detail panel. The cost is at page scale, where the figure is read at roughly 900 px wide: the outline stays a pale hairline, and where it hugs the plasma edge its gaps close up, so the component this node's done-when is about is the least legible mark in the scene and is read partly by inference from the legend. A stronger lightness step from the coil grey, or a wider dash period, would separate it without thinning anything else. Non-blocking because the contour is traceable end to end within the scene and the legend names it.

The scene draws the same plasma twice at two extents — an overview carrying the fourteen coil sections, and a wall-only detail — and names neither. build_figure draws the two panels with no title, panel label or annotation, and the evidence caption at docs/evidence/fragments/sub-millisecond-forward-path/iter-bank-recertify.html:92 describes 'the regenerated panel' in the singular. On the delivered raster a reader sees two plasma outlines of different sizes with nothing saying how they relate, so the right-hand panel can read as a second plasma state rather than the magnified wall-and-cell detail of the same mesh. Naming each panel, or one caption sentence saying the right panel is the detail, removes the inference; nothing here stops a reader using either panel, so this does not hold the node.

The evidence table describes the first wall as a 'dashed dark grey #9aa2ab', but on the delivered raster #9aa2ab is the lightest ink in the figure at 2.583:1 against white — below the 3:1 the repository's style asks of a line on white and lighter than the coil grey it is set against (3.112:1). The word 'dark' overstates the separation, and this is the line a reader checks to decide how visible the wall is; 'light blue-grey dash' states what the picture shows. The same paragraph's claim that the wall sits 'above the clipped plasma-cell outlines' is accurate and visible in the raster. The picture is not changed by this — the record's description of it is.
